title: RowDrag.settle walks the grabbed row past every neighbour whose crossing threshold it has passed, folding each slot shift into the compensation
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/RowDrag.swift:41-77 settle - guards on `let id, let index = order.firstIndex(of: id)`; `let own = heights[id] ?? fallbackHeight`; loop: downward when `offset > 0, current + 1 < order.count` with `let slot = heights[next] ?? fallbackHeight` and `guard offset > (own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre, move(next, true) else { break }` then `settled += slot; current += 1; moved = true`; upward mirrored with `-offset` and `settled -= slot`; returns `moved`
DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/RowDrag.swift:36 - `pastCentre: CGFloat = 0` default
DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:782-801 dragChanged - calls `drag.settle(order:heights:fallbackHeight: Chrome.rowHeight + 1)` with no pastCentre
E:/Droppy/port/porting/port_impacts.md:316 entry 154 - the move callback returns Bool; break on false WITHOUT advancing index or compensation; strict `>`; fallbackHeight = rowHeight + 1 = 29
preconditions: A row is grabbed and a pointer move has been delivered.
action: The visual offset exceeds half the sum of the grabbed row's slot and the next neighbour's slot, in either direction.
expected_result: The neighbour and the grabbed row swap. The test is a strict greater-than against `(own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre`, with pastCentre zero in the sidebar, so the swap fires the moment the centre is crossed. The loop repeats, so one fast flick can cross several rows in a single delivery. If the move closure returns false the loop breaks without advancing the index and without adding the compensation. Each accepted swap adds or subtracts the neighbour's slot height from `settled`, which keeps the row pinned under the pointer while the list flows around it. The compensation must be applied inside `settle`, not inside the move closure, because `settle` mutates a copy of the caller's state.
side_effects: Each accepted swap writes the model through the move closure.
failure_cases: Grabbed id not in `order`: returns false immediately and nothing moves.
Move refused: loop stops there, leaving earlier swaps in place.
windows_path: Direct translation of the arithmetic. A void-returning move callback would reorder forever past a refused move (port_impacts 154), so the Bool return is mandatory. The fallback height is the literal 29 (Chrome.rowHeight 28 plus the list's 1 pt spacing).
verification_method: unit test on RowDrag.settle covering multi-row flicks, a refused move, a missing id and both directions.

title: The reorder slot's head-card fallback uses six glyphs per row and omits the chevron row, disagreeing with the card's own layout
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:846-848 slotHeights - `let rows = (headCount + 5) / 6`

DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:1453 HeadCardsRow - `let perRow = width == 0 ? 7 : max(1, Int((usable + ThreadRowMetrics.headGlyphPitch - ThreadRowMetrics.headGlyphSize) / ThreadRowMetrics.headGlyphPitch))`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:1463 - `let cardRows = rows.count + (capped ? 1 : 0)`
E:/Droppy/port/porting/upstream_defects.md:131 entry 59
preconditions: A thread with seven or more heads, or more than twelve heads, whose card height has not yet been measured.
expected_result: The fallback under-measures: it assumes six glyphs per row while the card lays out at seven per row until measured, and it omits the extra glyph row the card adds for the show-all chevron when there are more than twelve heads. The crossing thresholds are therefore slightly wrong until the real height lands in the measured-height table under `heads-<uuid>`, after which both agree. This is an upstream defect and both formulas are reproduced verbatim and separately; they are not unified.
failure_cases: Visible as a slightly early or late swap on the first drag after the card appears.
windows_path: Copy both formulas verbatim, including the six-per-row fallback, the seven-per-row unmeasured default and the missing chevron row (port_impacts entry 177).
verification_method: unit test asserting the two formulas disagree for headCount 7 and for headCount 13, exactly as the source does.

title: A project-layout reorder writes sortOrder on every open thread of the project and makes the moved thread inherit the target's pinned flag
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:337-352 moveThread(_:to:placeAfter:) - guards `id != targetID`, both threads exist, same projectID, project exists, neither is settled; builds `before` from `threads(in: project).filter { !$0.isSettled }.map(\.id)`; removes and re-inserts at `placeAfter ? index + 1 : index`; `guard order != before else { return false }`; `updateThreads(order) { position, thread in if thread.id == id { thread.isPinned = target.isPinned }; thread.sortOrder = Double(position) }`; returns true
preconditions: Project layout; a thread dragged past a neighbour in the same project.
expected_result: Every open thread of that project is rewritten with `sortOrder` equal to its zero-based position in the new order, and the moved thread's `isPinned` is set to the target's, so dragging an unpinned thread above a pinned one pins it and dragging a pinned thread below an unpinned one unpins it. The call returns false and writes nothing when the ids are equal, when either thread is settled, when they are in different projects, or when the resulting order is unchanged.
side_effects: Writes the library through updateThreads, which schedules a save.
persistence: thread.sortOrder (Double?) and thread.isPinned (Bool) are persisted in the library for every open thread of the project.
failure_cases: Any guard fails: returns false, RowDrag breaks its loop without compensating.
windows_path: Direct translation; the Bool return feeds RowDrag's break (port_impacts entry 154).
verification_method: contract fixture asserting the rewritten sortOrder array and the inherited pin, plus a restart test.

title: An activity-layout reorder writes activityOrder and activityOrderDay on every thread of the group
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:356-370 moveInActivity(_:to:placeAfter:among:) - guards `id != targetID, peers.contains(id), peers.contains(targetID)`; re-inserts in the peers array; `guard order != peers else { return false }`; `let calendar = Calendar.current`; `updateThreads(order) { position, thread in thread.activityOrder = Double(position); thread.activityOrderDay = calendar.startOfDay(for: thread.updatedAt) }`
preconditions: Activity layout; a thread dragged past a neighbour in the same section.
expected_result: Every thread in the group gets `activityOrder` equal to its zero-based position and `activityOrderDay` set to the start of the day of that thread's own `updatedAt`, not of the moved thread's. Unlike the project reorder, the pinned flag is not touched, so dragging into or out of the Pinned section does not pin or unpin.
persistence: thread.activityOrder (Double?) and thread.activityOrderDay (Date?) are persisted for every thread of the group.
failure_cases: Ids equal, either not in peers, or order unchanged: returns false and writes nothing.
windows_path: Direct translation; start-of-day uses the user's local calendar.
verification_method: contract fixture asserting per-thread activityOrderDay from each thread's own updatedAt, plus a restart test.

title: Hovering a thread, helper or head row pre-decodes that thread's history
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:1816-1820 SidebarThreadRow - `.onHover { hovering in withAnimation(Chrome.hover) { isHovering = hovering }; if hovering { model.warmDocuments([thread.id]) } }`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:1386-1389 SidebarHelperRow - the same
DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:1494-1497 HeadCardsRow glyph - the same for the head
DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:440-445 warmDocuments - `let cold = ids.filter { runtimes[$0] == nil }; guard !cold.isEmpty else { return }; DocumentPrefetch.shared.warm(cold)`
expected_result: The thread's history is decoded off the main thread if no runtime already exists for it, so opening the thread costs no parse on the click. Threads already open are skipped. Hover leaving does not cancel the prefetch.
side_effects: Reads the thread's document from disk on a background queue.
failure_cases: Runtime already exists: nothing is scheduled.
cancellation: The prefetch itself is not cancelled by hover exit.
windows_path: Background file read on the Windows thread pool; must not block the UI thread and must not hold a lock the selection path needs.
verification_method: interaction test asserting a prefetch is scheduled on hover and not for an open thread.
